$comment: Per-class asset budgets for Project Bravo. tools/bake.mjs targets these;
tools/verify.mjs fails the build when an output exceeds one.
Texture sizes are chosen from how large the object actually gets on screen, not
from what Meshy happened to export. A sword occupies roughly 30 pixels in the
player's hand; a 2048px albedo for it is about 40x more texel than the screen can
ever show, and costs ~22 MB of VRAM to hold.
maxBytes is the on-disk ceiling for the baked .glb and is deliberately generous:
it is a backstop against a runaway asset, not the primary control. Texture

classes.name: prop
classes.reason: Held in-hand or placed set dressing. Never more than a few dozen pixels tall on screen.

classes.name: wearable
classes.reason: Armour worn on the character. Read at character distance, but only ever covers part of the body.

classes.name: character
classes.reason: Player, NPCs and mobs. The things players actually look at, and the only class that earns 1024px.

classes.name: structure
classes.reason: Buildings and large world geometry. Big on screen, but static and seen from a distance.

default.name: unclassified
default.reason: No rule matched. Treated as a prop so nothing ships unbudgeted by accident; add a rule above if that is wrong.

totals.$comment: Whole-payload ceilings, checked by verify.mjs across the baked directory.
